result.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
result.summary: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided reconstruction raises the mean functional score, the cycle-weighted share of passed cases, from 24.6% to 30.9%. Of the 58 fully passing designs, only three improve on the reference's combined power, area, and delay, so behavioral recovery and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ChiProgramBench：从开源处理器、加速器等电路构造 18 个任务，令 LLM agent 仅通过驱动和读取隐藏有状态参考电路引脚来做实验、推测功能与时序，并提交门级网表；在 6 种 agent 配置的 432 次试验中，全用例通过率仅 12.0%（黑盒）与 14.8%（功能引导），且少有设计同时改善功耗、面积与延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「实验探测隐藏状态—假设—被观测反驳—重建」的闭环，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据获取、动态计算分配与停止决策提供问题表述线索；但任务域与多模态推理相距较远，实际可迁移性需阅读原文核查。
